text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

## Abstract
This inquiry examined whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 refer to the same GEO study. Using accession-based queries, data revealed that these identifiers represent different GEO record types: GSE309890 is a GEO Series, while GDS309890 is a GEO DataSet. Both are linked to distinct FTP directories and GEO URLs. This differentiation clarifies potential confusion in usage.

## I. Introduction
### Background
GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) repositories categorize their records into Series (GSE), Platforms (GPL), Samples (GSM), and DataSets (GDS). Series encompass experimental data sets submitted by researchers, whereas DataSets are curated subsets of Series designed for easy reuse.

### Literature Review
No literature was retrieved for this query, as the focus lies on database-level clarification.

### Knowledge Gap
Confusion often arises between similarly numbered Series and DataSets due to partial overlap in experimental data and their accession numbers.

### Objective & Hypothesis
To determine if GSE309890 and GDS309890 represent the same GEO entry.

## II. Materials and Methods
### Study Design
Verify the type and corresponding metadata for GSE309890 and GDS309890.

### Materials
Geo Resolve Accession Tool

### Procedures
- Query both "GSE309890" and "GDS309890" for their metadata using the `geo_resolve_accession` tool.
- Analyze the record type, UID conversion rule, and associated FTP and GEO pages.

### Statistical Analysis
This is a verification study, so no statistical methods were applied.

## III. Results
### Data Presentation
| Accession ID | UID        | Type | FTP Directory                                                 | GEO URL                                                   |
|--------------|------------|------|--------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890    | 200309890  | GSE  | [GSE FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/) | [GSE Page](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890) |
| GDS309890    | 309890     | GDS  | [GDS FTP](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/) | [GDS Page](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890) |

### Findings
The identifiers correspond to:
- **GSE309890**: GEO Series
- **GDS309890**: GEO DataSet

## IV. Discussion
### Interpretation
GSE309890 and GDS309890 are distinct entries. While GDS309890 may derive from data in GSE309890, they serve differing functional purposes.

### Context
The UID conversion rule confirms type-specific handling (Series prepends "2", DataSet has no digit).

### Limitations
This analysis does not investigate the experimental overlap or reuse between GSE and GDS records.

### Conclusion & Future Directions
GSE309890 and GDS309890 differ in their roles within GEO. Future work might explore data reuse pathways from Series to curated DataSets.

## References
1. GEO Accession Resolution Tool - [GSE309890](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890)
2. GEO Accession Resolution Tool - [GDS309890](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890)

## Acknowledgments
NCBI GEO for accession metadata and resolution service.
